releases.description:
## GridSense 0.16.0

- **Columns now follow the order your properties appear in your notes**, instead of an internal usage order. Filling in values never reshuffles them.
- **Reset column order**: dragging headers is still remembered per grid, and the columns manager now tells you whether a custom order is in effect and offers "Reset to note order".
- **Jump to column**: a ⇥ column button (also Mod+G, and a command) opens a type-to-search picker and scrolls the grid straight to that column — no more dragging the scrollbar across a wide grid. It lands the column clear of any frozen columns.
- **Views in the toolbar**: saved views now have a dropdown next to the filter box — switch between them, save the current setup, or open the manager. Applying a view now replaces the whole setup, so a setting the view doesn't specify (like a sort) no longer leaks in from the view you were just on.

releases.description:
## GridSense 0.15.2

- New command: **Scan folder for blank or duplicate notes** — lists empty notes and genuine look-alike name groups (with sizes and timestamps) for the current grid's folder, and copies a full report to the clipboard. Built to capture evidence if a stray blank note ever appears.
- The spreadsheet importer now tells you when a pasted row's name already existed and it created a numbered note instead, rather than doing it silently.

releases.description:
## GridSense 0.15.0

**Fixes**

- Links to notes that don't exist now look unresolved (faded, dashed) instead of like normal links.
- Fill down/right on many cells now locks the grid read-only, shows a progress notice saying so, keeps your scroll position, and repaints once at the end instead of flickering.
- Editing a cell no longer makes its row vanish from an active filter mid-edit — filtered rows stay put until you change the filter or refresh.
- The floating new-row bar no longer leaves a sliver of the last row showing underneath it.
- Column headers are now guaranteed to stay above frozen rows while scrolling.

**New**

- **Stacked filters** (⛃ filters): build up property conditions with all/any matching, like Bases — the quick filter box still narrows whatever they leave.
- The filter box has a clear (✕) button.
- **Bases Toolbox property tools** appear in the column header menu and columns manager when that plugin is installed: format doctor, property index, allowed-value and alias audits, fork/convert, duplicate finder, inline-field migration, rollups, metadata stamp.
- The properties switch button now names only the mode you'd switch to, and hides Obsidian's redundant "Properties" title while it's shown.

releases.description:
## GridSense 0.14.0

A big batch from a round of real-world use. Highlights:

**Grid**

- **Freeze panes**: pin the first N columns and/or rows while you scroll (▦ columns & views).
- **Hidden things are now obvious**: a red warning in the toolbar names how many columns are hidden and how many rows aren't shown, and opens the manager when clicked.
- **Set a column's width by typing it** — right-click the header → Set column width, or go back to automatic.
- Columns keep their order when you fill in values (they used to reshuffle), and new columns are always added at the end.
- Fill down/right no longer flickers — filled cells stay filled while Obsidian catches up.

**History**

- **Row, column and cell history**: right-click a row number, a column header or a cell to see just that item's edits, each with a one-click **restore**.

**Formulas**

- New formula columns: **COUNTIF, SUMIF, CONCAT, IF, IFS and AND**, built with a condition editor (=, ≠, >, <, ≥, ≤, contains, empty, not empty). CONCAT can join properties, file.basename/path/folder, and quoted literals.

**Import**

- **Import notes from a spreadsheet paste**: paste your cells, map columns to properties, preview, then create the notes — nothing is written until you say so, and the raw paste is saved as a CSV first in case you want to redo it.

**Files & notes**

- **.grid files**: save a folder's grid as a document (folder menu → Save as .grid file) and open it like any other file.
- The properties panel takeover can now be switched **per note** as well as globally, with commands for both.
- Many grid actions are now commands you can bind hotkeys to: fill down/right, find & replace, undo/redo, word wrap, add column, columns & views, history, recompile, import, empty trash.

releases.description:
## GridSense 0.9.0

- **Grid config can now live in your vault.** Per-grid setup (columns, widths, sort, filters, views, formulas) is normally stored in the plugin's data.json, which only travels if you sync your .obsidian folder. Turn on **Store grid config in the vault** to mirror it into a normal vault file that syncs alongside your notes — and a newer copy arriving from another device is picked up live.
- **Deleting a row is now undoable.** Row deletes move the note into a GridSense trash folder inside your vault (browsable, restorable, ⌘Z brings it straight back) instead of going straight to Obsidian's trash. A new command, **Empty GridSense trash**, hands everything to Obsidian's trash when you're ready. Folder name is configurable.
- Wikilinks typed in cells are tidied automatically: extra brackets like `[[[[Note]]]]` collapse to `[[Note]]`, both while typing and on save.

releases.description:
## GridSense 0.8.0

**Fixes**

- Columns no longer reshuffle when you fill in values — column order is stable, and newly added columns go to the end.
- Fill down/right no longer flickers: filled cells stay filled instead of blanking out and restoring while Obsidian re-indexes.
- Right-clicking a multi-cell selection keeps the selection (it used to collapse to one cell, which is why fill from the menu worked but the hotkey complained).
- Clicking inside a cell you're editing no longer kicks you out of edit mode.
- The floating new-row form can no longer cover the last data row.

**New**

- Internal links render as real links in cells, including aliases (`[[Note|shown text]]`), and cell editing offers note autocomplete after you type `[[`.
- Right-click a row number to delete that note (moved to trash, with a confirmation).
- Per-grid column width cap in ▦ columns & views.
- Property-type icons in the columns manager.
- A button above the note properties panel switches between GridSense's editor and Obsidian's, both ways, without a trip to settings.

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
## GridSense 0.7.0

- Paste straight from Excel, Google Sheets, Numbers, or LibreOffice: cells containing newlines and quotes now paste correctly (spreadsheets wrap such cells in quotes — the grid unwraps them instead of shredding rows), and Windows/unicode row separators are handled. No importer needed.
- New ＋ header at the right edge of the grid: click, type a property name (with autocomplete over properties used in this folder and across your vault), Enter — the column is added to every note, undoable. Also available with autocomplete in the columns manager.
- Fixed: keyboard shortcuts (undo, fill down/right, find & replace) now work in pop-out windows.

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
## GridSense 0.6.0

- Clearing cells no longer deletes properties: emptying a cell (Delete, find & replace, clearing a column) keeps the property with an empty value. Only explicit delete actions remove keys.
- Fixed: the first and last rows of the grid couldn't really be edited (typing took one character, double-click did nothing) — the sticky top draft row was overlapping them. The top draft now scrolls with the grid and looks identical to the bottom one.
- Right-click a row number (or the note link): duplicate the note (\"name (copy)\") or rename it — renames update links vault-wide.
- Add column: header right-click or the columns manager — adds a property (empty) to every note in the grid, undoable.
- Delete column: header right-click, with a confirmation warning that it removes the property and values from all notes in the grid — undoable while the tab is open, and always in the edit log.
- Formulas from the note properties strip: add/edit folder formulas right where you edit a note's properties; they render computed (ƒ, never written to notes) and appear as columns on the folder's grid automatically.

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
## GridSense 0.5.0

- Empty draft rows at the top and bottom of every grid. Drafts are UI-only: no note is created until the row has a name and you press Enter — then the note is created, any property values you typed flush into it, and a fresh draft appears. Abandoning or clearing a draft never touches your files, and clearing cells in a real row never deletes the note.
- Excel-style row stability: once displayed, row order is frozen — editing cells (even the sorted column) and newly created notes never reshuffle the grid. Changing sort, filter, or pressing ↺ re-derives the order. Notes committed from a draft stay pinned to the end of the grid where you made them.
- Fixed: a background recompile could drop its follow-up refresh, leaving the grid on stale rows.

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
## GridSense 0.4.3

- New setting: default row limit — applied to every grid that has no per-folder limit (0 = unlimited, the default). Per-folder limits in ▦ columns & views override it; clearing the folder field falls back to the plugin default. The row counter always shows when a limit is trimming.

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
## GridSense 0.4.2

- Removed the silent default row cap (was 2,000): a fresh grid now always shows every note in scope, so you never mistake a truncated grid for the whole folder. Virtualized rendering keeps big folders fast.
- Prominent row counter in the toolbar: "1,234 rows", or "60 of 1,234 rows" (highlighted) whenever a filter or row limit is trimming the view — with a tooltip saying which.
- Grids over 10,000 rows show a warning button that opens the columns & views modal to hide columns or set a row limit.

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
## GridSense 0.4.1

- Inline properties takeover is now OFF by default while in beta (Settings toggle).
- Property rows have a type button on the left: change property type (Text/List/Number/Checkbox/Date/Date & time), zoom the value, or delete — reserved properties (tags, aliases, cssclasses) are recognized and locked to their list types.
- Values parse by property type: tags strip #, lists split on commas or newlines, numbers and checkboxes coerce properly.
- List values render as chips with a visible x per item (removal is undoable).
- Left/right arrows switch between key and value (same as Tab).
- Fixed: double-clicking a value no longer kicks you out of edit mode; Tab after editing stays in the properties strip instead of jumping to the note body.
- New: cell zoom — a large editor for one value, in the property menu and the grid's right-click menu.

## GridSense 0.4.0

- Inline frontmatter takeover: Obsidian's native properties panel is replaced by GridSense's keyboard-friendly editor in Live Preview and Reading mode (toggle in settings; on by default). Arrow keys navigate, Tab switches key/value, Enter edits, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter adds, Cmd/Ctrl+Backspace deletes, Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes.
- The properties modal and inline editor now share one component.
- README: install from the community plugin store.
